title: High Press Trigger
content: A high press is a coordinated team movement to win possession high up the pitch, immediately after a pressing trigger occurs. Triggers include: a goalkeeper receiving a back-pass under no pressure, a center-back receiving with their back to goal, or a misplaced pass by the opposition. When the trigger fires, the nearest attacker immediately presses the ball carrier, with teammates cutting off passing lanes to force the ball carrier to play long or make an error. The press must be coordinated — if only one player presses without teammates cutting lanes, the opposition plays through easily. Key principle: press to a corner or sideline, where the ball carrier has fewer escape routes.
example_questions: What specific moment should we all rush forward to win the ball back high up the pitch?
The goalkeeper just caught the ball and is looking to pass to a defender, so should I start running toward him?
As a striker, how do I know if I should press the center-back or stay back when they receive the ball?
We keep waiting too long to press and let them settle into their shape, so what is the best signal for us to start the press?
